title: Localization-compatible affine charts for an arbitrary-open integral map
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $j:U\hookrightarrow S$ be an arbitrary open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion], and let $g:V\to U$ be an integral morphism [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. For every affine open $W=\operatorname{Spec}(A)\subseteq S$, after refining $W\cap U$ by a principal affine open cover $W_i=D(f_i)$ with $V_i=g^{-1}(W_i)=\operatorname{Spec}(B_i)$, let $C_i$ be the integral closure of $A$ in $B_i$. The canonical localization identifications $(C_i)_{f_i f_j}\cong(C_j)_{f_i f_j}$ on every affine overlap are induced by localization of integral closure. They satisfy the cocycle condition, so the affine schemes $\operatorname{Spec}(C_i)$ glue compatibly as $W$ and the affine cover vary; the resulting glued scheme is integral over $S$ and restricts over $U$ to $V$.

source.place: Stacks Project, Morphisms Lemma 0CNX (lemma-extend-integral-surjective-morphisms), proof; Morphisms Lemmas 035F and 035K for localization-compatible charts

proof.text: Fix an affine open $W=\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ of $S$ and a principal affine cover $W\cap U=\bigcup_iD(f_i)$, with $V_i=V\times_U D(f_i)=\operatorname{Spec}(B_i)$. Since $g$ is integral, the induced map $A_{f_i}\to B_i$ is integral. Regard $A\to B_i$ through $A\to A_{f_i}$ and define $C_i\subseteq B_i$ to be the integral closure of $A$ in $B_i$. This produces an affine chart $\operatorname{Spec}(C_i)\to\operatorname{Spec}(A)$, integral by the definition of integral closure and of an integral affine morphism.

source.place: Tag 0CNX proof, affine normalization charts; Morphisms Section 29.54

proof.text: On the overlap $D(f_if_j)$, the localization theorem for integral closure identifies $(C_i)_{f_if_j}$ with the integral closure of $A_{f_if_j}$ in $(B_i)_{f_if_j}$. Because $A_{f_i}\to B_i$ is integral, every element of $B_i$ is integral over $A_{f_i}$, so after localizing at $f_j$ this closure is $(B_i)_{f_j}$. The same calculation from the $j$-chart gives $(B_j)_{f_i}$, and the two are canonically identified with the restriction of $V$ to the common principal open. Localization is transitive, so these identifications agree on triple overlaps and obey the cocycle condition.

source.place: Morphisms Lemma 035K (normalization-localization), together with Tag 0307; more-morphisms.tex Tag 0CNX proof

proof.text: Apply the scheme-gluing theorem to the schemes $\operatorname{Spec}(C_i)$, their principal-open overlap subschemes, and the transition isomorphisms from Step 2. The identity, inverse, and triple-overlap equations just checked are precisely its gluing-data hypotheses. The glued scheme $V_W$ has open affine charts mapping to $W$; each chart ring $C_i$ is integral over $A$, hence $V_W\to W$ is integral, and its restriction over $W\cap U$ is identified with $V\times_U(W\cap U)$ by the localized chart identifications.

If $W'$ is another affine open of $S$, the constructions on $W$ and $W'$ restrict to the same charts on every affine principal refinement of $W\cap W'$, by the localization identifications of Step 2. The resulting chart isomorphisms satisfy the same cocycle condition, so the $V_W$ glue over an affine cover of $S$ to a scheme $V'\to S$. Integrality is affine-local on the target and therefore survives this gluing. On $U$ the localized charts are exactly the given $V_i$, so the base change $V'\times_SU$ is canonically isomorphic to $V$ over $U$.

Existing DAG leaves for integral-closure localization and scheme gluing suffice, so no new nodes were created.
